scope: READ THE CODEC: -97 is a one-bit gate followed by EITHER 32 bits OR 8 bits, and the 8-bit form is a signed offset from a baseline

the_reader_0x66f9e0.0x66F9F3: jne 0x66FA0B    -> gate == 1: read the full 32 bits
the_reader_0x66f9e0.0x66FA01: sub edi,eax     -> value = baseline - the 8-bit reading
the_reader_0x66f9e0.0x66FA0B: gate == 1: read 4 bytes and return them

the_cost.note: both forms are FIXED width - neither depends on the value's magnitude

what_this_explains: why 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 and 255 all cost exactly 55 bits: with gate=1 they all take the 33-bit form, so the total is constant
it does NOT yet explain the 97-bit runs (values 6 and 5830), because those wrote the same gate=1 + 32 bits and should also cost 33
the_hypothesis_for_the_97_bit_runs: those two runs are exactly the ones where the ps parse ERRORED, so the 97 is where the decoder STOPPED, not a valid field cost
so the question is what makes the decode fail for those two values - and since the field itself is fixed width, the failure is more likely downstream (the next-iteration prologue we pad with zeros)
6 (0b110) and 5830 (0b1011011000110) both have BIT 0 CLEAR, while 255, 256, 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096 all have BIT 0 SET or are single-bit
that is now a concrete, checkable distinction
next: test value 7 (0b111, bit 0 set, close to 6) and value 5 (0b101, bit 0 set)
if they parse cleanly while 6 does not, the bit-0 distinction is confirmed and it points at a downstream reader, not at the codec
